comments.body:
SCOPE DECISION BY THE OPERATOR: the rate limiter IS in scope for epic e369. Re-parented under the epic
and re-typed as a story.

I had argued this was an absent FEATURE rather than a defect — off by default, DC-only, admin-enabled.
The operator's counter is the stronger one and I should have weighted it higher: an integration that
falls over on a rate-limited instance is broken FOR THAT CUSTOMER, and 'the admin has to enable it' is
a thin defence when Data Center exists precisely for large self-hosted deployments — the ones most
likely to turn throttling on.

Scope is unchanged from the bug description: honour Retry-After when present, with up to 20% random
jitter per Atlassian's guidance, and treat ABSENT headers as normal (limiter off / pre-8.6 / Server).
No static pacing policy — the limit is admin-configured and unknowable to us.

VERIFY THE NUMBERS BEFORE BUILDING TO THEM: 'off by default', '8.6+', and 'retry-after + 20% jitter'
come from the OSS research with Atlassian citations, not from my own testing, and that research
retracted two of its other claims on a second pass. Confirm against the target DC version.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN REWRITTEN ACROSS 9 REVIEW ROUNDS — still BLOCK as of this comment (round 10 in flight). The
plan is now materially different from the one this ticket started with, and the differences are the
point, so they are recorded here rather than left in the diff.

WHAT THE ROUNDS ACTUALLY CAUGHT (each verified in source before I accepted it)

 1. ROUND 1 (BLOCKING, G6) — the plan would have built a THIRD `Retry-After` implementation.
    `_errors.parse_retry_after()` (`_errors.py:32`) and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S = 60.0`
    (`_errors.py:29`) already exist, `dispatch_one.py:41` already imports both, and
    `dispatch_one.py:150-171` is ALREADY a 429-honouring retry path for the REST transport. The plan
    now reuses them and cites that path as the sibling to read first.

 2. ROUND 4 (BLOCKING, G6) — THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. The plan routed 429 retries through
    `_with_connection_retry`, which is the transport's single choke point for ALL 15 call sites,
    INCLUDING `create_issue`/`add_comment`/`add_label`. Its docstring already states the policy and
    the reason: JIRAError is unretried because "retrying a mutation on an HTTP error risks
    duplicates". The plan as written would have REINTRODUCED THE DUPLICATE-ISSUE CLASS THAT
    [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] JUST FIXED. Now: 429 retry is scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS; mutations
    keep today's fail-fast, because a 429 can arrive after the server began the write and nothing in
    the response distinguishes that from rejection at the gate. The opt-in defaults to OFF so a
    mutation added later cannot inherit it by omission.

 3. ROUND 6 (BLOCKING) — the opt-in mechanism could not reach most of the reads. `_call_logged`
    wraps `_with_connection_retry` (`:287`), and most reads route through it, so a parameter on the
    inner wrapper alone was unreachable for them. `_call_logged` now forwards the same flag.

 4. ROUND 6 also found `get_comment_map` has TWO network layers — besides the shared pager it
    fetches per-issue comments at `:473` through a bare `_with_connection_retry`. That is ONE REQUEST
    PER ISSUE, i.e. the highest-volume read in a pass and the likeliest thing to be rate limited, and
    my "three map readers covered by opting in one helper" left exactly it uncovered.

 5. ROUND 6/7 — `probe_remote` calls `_with_connection_retry` DIRECTLY (`:493`), so grouping it with
    the `_call_logged` members made its opt-in structurally unreachable.

 6. ROUND 9 — `transition_issue_by_name`'s READ leg (`transitions()`, `:373`) is a pure read I had
    silently omitted. Fixing it sharpened the rule: THE BOUNDARY IS PER-CALL, NOT PER-METHOD — that
    method's read leg opts in and its write leg (`:384`) does not.

TWO REVIEWER CLAIMS I FIRST SCORED AS WRONG, AND WAS WRONG TO — both have the SAME root cause, and
it is worth carrying forward: **the plan reviewer reads `origin/main`, not this story's base.**
 * "`_paged_search` does not exist" (raised 4x). It DOES — `transport.py:421` — but it arrives with
   [rebar:9263-b404-cb6c-463f], which is in review as change 1129 and NOT on main
   (`git show origin/main:...transport.py | grep -c _paged_search` -> 0). The finding was right about
   the tree it reads. The plan now declares the 9263 dependency explicitly, with that command as the
   check.
 * "transport.py is 792 LOC, not 789". BOTH are right: `origin/main` is 792, the post-9263 base is
   789, and the 3-line delta IS 9263's pager consolidation. I rejected this in round 1 on a bare
   `wc -l` of my own tree without noticing the reviewer reads a different one. The plan now names
   both numbers and which base each applies to.

MY OWN RECURRING FAILURE, recorded because it cost 3 of the 9 rounds: I fixed one section and left
another contradicting it (Scope vs Approach on `_call_logged`; an AC citing `:168` after the Approach
corrected it to `:169`). That is exactly the "grep the WHOLE document for the term you changed"
lesson from handoff #4, and I did not apply it consistently.

DESIGN DECISIONS NOW PINNED IN THE PLAN
 * Order of operations: jitter FIRST, clamp LAST — `min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, retry_after * (1 +
   random.uniform(0, 0.2)))`. Clamp-last is what makes an oversized value land on exactly 60s;
   jitter-last would give 60-72 and contradict the AC.
 * An oversized `Retry-After` is CLAMPED (matching `dispatch_one.py:166`), not a hard failure — a
   second divergent policy for one signal is what the blocking finding was about.
 * `Retry-After: 0` parses to `0.0`, NOT None (`return secs if secs >= 0 else None`), so it is an
   immediate retry bounded by the cap. An earlier draft claimed the helper returned None for 0.
 * The header is read from `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`. Verified at runtime against
   pycontribs 3.10.5: `JIRAError.__init__` takes `(text, status_code, url, request, response)` and
   sets BOTH `self.response` and `self.headers` (the latter from **kwargs, typically None). Reading
   the wrong one returns None even when the header is present — a silent always-falls-back failure.
 * Placement: `transport.py` is at the LOCKED 800 cap, so the retry/error cluster extracts to
   `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — and `TlsVerificationError` MUST move with it, or
   `_tls_verification_error` (which instantiates it at `:218`) creates a circular import.
   `transport.py` re-exports the moved names so `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py:183-184`, which
   reaches both through the module object, keeps passing UNEDITED.

NOT STARTED: no code has been written for this ticket. The plan must reach a certified attestation
before it can be claimed.

comments.body:
ROUND 10: BLOCK, and the finding count went UP (7+ blocking, vs 1 in round 9). That reverses the
trend and is itself the signal — applying handoff #4's lesson 3: WHEN A PLAN KEEPS RETURNING
DOUBLE-DIGIT FINDINGS, SUSPECT STRUCTURE, NOT WORDING. J9 blocked 8 times in this epic and splitting
it into J10 produced a first-try PASS.

MY RECOMMENDATION TO WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: **SPLIT THIS TICKET IN TWO before spending round 11.**
This plan is carrying two independent changes, which is why every round finds new surface:

  S1 — EXTRACT the retry/error cluster from `transport.py` into `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`.
       Pure, behaviour-preserving relocation forced by the LOCKED 800-LOC cap. Includes
       `TlsVerificationError` (or `_tls_verification_error` at `:218` creates a circular import) and
       re-exports so `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py:183-184` pass UNEDITED. Verifiable by a diff
       read and two `wc -l`. Depends on 9263.

  S2 — ADD the 429 policy in the extracted module: reuse `_errors.parse_retry_after` /
       `MAX_BACKOFF_S`, jitter-then-clamp, and the per-CALL read/mutation opt-in.

The rounds show exactly why they should not ship together: rounds 1, 4, 8, 9 and 10 were all about
S2's POLICY (reuse, duplicate-risk scoping, citation precision, per-call boundary, cap-exhaustion
behaviour), while rounds 6-7 were about S1's MECHANICS (what moves, what routes through what, which
tree the LOC is measured on). Each round the two interleave and a fix to one re-opens surface in the
other. Split, and S1 becomes a one-pass mechanical review.

ROUND 10'S FINDINGS, for whoever continues (verify each against `origin/main`, not your branch):
 1. [G6, GENUINELY IMPORTANT AND UNANSWERED] The plan never says WHAT EXCEPTION ESCAPES when the
    429 retry cap is exhausted. Re-raising the raw `JIRAError` would leak a vendor type straight
    past the adapter boundary that `_as_backend_http_error` exists to seal — callers catch
    `BackendHTTPError`. This is a real design hole, not wording, and it is the single best argument
    that S2 deserves its own focused review.
 2. [G6] HOW `_paged_search` opts in is ambiguous: does it always pass `rate_limit_retry=True`, or
    accept and forward a flag from its callers? Opposite failure modes.
 3. [E4] Whether `_paged_search` routes through `_call_logged` is asserted from 9263's PLAN TEXT,
    not from landed code — because 9263 is not on main yet. Re-verify once 1129 lands.
 4. [COH] Scope says "ELEVEN read call sites"; the table has TEN rows. My own arithmetic error.
 5. [G1G2] The mutation AC uses an ellipsis ("create_issue, add_comment, add_label, …") where the
    transport has ~10 distinct non-opting mutation sites; enumerate them rather than gesture.

DO NOT treat 1, 2 and 5 as wording fixes. 1 in particular changes what the code does.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROUND 10'S OPEN ITEMS, RESOLVED AGAINST LANDED CODE — recording before the split so S1/S2 start from
facts rather than from plan text.

FINDING 1 (the design hole: WHAT ESCAPES WHEN THE 429 RETRY CAP IS EXHAUSTED). **Answer:
`BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429` — never the raw `JIRAError`.** This is not a preference, it is
what the existing boundary already does and what J10 pinned. `_with_connection_retry` catches
`_jira_http_error_types()` and does `raise _as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc`
(transport.py:243-246 region), and `_as_backend_http_error` reads `.status_code` into
`BackendHTTPError.code` using urllib's spelling SO THAT the core's existing
`except urllib.error.HTTPError` branches classify a DC failure exactly as they classify a Cloud one
— e.g. a 404 read reaching `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` is seen as `_DELETED`.
So the requirement on S2 is precise and testable: the exhausted-cap path must funnel through the SAME
translation, yielding `BackendHTTPError(code=429)`. A test should assert the TYPE and the CODE, and
should also assert that `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` does NOT escape — the vendor type leaking past
the adapter boundary is the actual regression risk, and a test that only checks "it raised" would
pass while that happened. Note the degradation rule too: a library error with no usable status
becomes `code=0`, which no core branch mistakes for a 404 or a success.

FINDING 3 (asserted from 9263's PLAN TEXT, not landed code — "re-verify once 1129 lands"). **1129 HAS
LANDED; re-verified on `origin/main`: `_paged_search` DOES route through `_call_logged`.** It is
defined at transport.py:421 and its body calls `_call_logged(...)` wrapping
`self._client.search_issues(...)`. Its callers on main are the project reads (`:455`, `:469`) and the
parent-map read (`:567`). So the opt-in question in finding 2 is a real fork with a real target, not
a hypothetical.

TRANSPORT SIZE, measured rather than remembered: `transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`**
right now, against the LOCKED 800 cap — ELEVEN lines of headroom. That is the fact that forces S1:
the 429 policy cannot be added in place. (Recording the number and its source because this file's LOC
has been misquoted twice in this epic — the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263
base difference, and now that 9263 is merged the two readings have converged at 789.)

CARRY-OVER FOR S2's PLAN, unchanged from round 10 and still unaddressed: finding 2 (does
`_paged_search` always opt in, or accept and forward a flag — opposite failure modes) and finding 5
(enumerate the ~10 non-opting mutation sites instead of an ellipsis). Finding 4 was my own
arithmetic error: Scope says ELEVEN read call sites, the table has TEN rows.

never a raw `JIRAError` — that is what `_as_backend_http_error` already does and what J10's neutral

verified on `origin/main` post-9263 (round 10 could only assert it from plan text).

compiled_state.description:
# DC rate-limit headers are not honoured; a 429 is a hard failure

## Context / Problem

Jira Data Center has built-in rate limiting (Administration → System → Rate limiting), introduced in
**8.6**, **Data Center only**, and **OFF BY DEFAULT** — an administrator enables it. It is a per-user
TOKEN BUCKET with a fill rate, not a fixed window.

rebar's DC transport does not handle it at all. `_with_connection_retry` retries only
connection-level faults and its docstring states explicitly that `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` — "any
HTTP 4xx/5xx response" — is NOT in the retry set. A 429 therefore propagates as a hard failure on
the first occurrence, aborting whatever read or mutation was in flight, on an instance that was
merely asking rebar to slow down.

**Scope decision by the operator:** this IS in scope for epic e369. The counter-argument that it is
an absent FEATURE rather than a defect (off by default, DC-only, admin-enabled) was weighed and
rejected: an integration that falls over on a rate-limited instance is broken FOR THAT CUSTOMER, and
"the admin has to enable it" is a thin defence when Data Center exists precisely for large
self-hosted deployments — the ones most likely to turn throttling on.

## Approach — THIS TICKET IS NOW A PARENT; THE WORK IS IN TWO CHILDREN

**This plan carried TWO independent changes and BLOCKED ten times because of it.** The full
round-by-round record is in this ticket's comments. The structural finding: rounds 6-7 were about
the MECHANICS of relocating code, while rounds 1, 4, 8, 9 and 10 were about the 429 POLICY, and each
round a fix to one re-opened surface in the other. Handoff lesson (epic e369): when a plan keeps
returning findings, suspect STRUCTURE, not wording — J9 blocked eight times and splitting it into
J10 produced a first-try PASS.

Split accordingly, and the implementation detail now lives in the children rather than here:

* **[rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] — S1: extract the retry/error cluster out of `transport.py`.** A
  pure, behaviour-preserving relocation, FORCED by the locked module-size cap: `transport.py` is
  789 lines against the 800 cap, so eleven lines of headroom mean the policy cannot be added in
  place. Verifiable by reading the diff and two `wc -l`. **PASSED plan review first try**, which is
  the evidence the split was the right move.
* **[rebar:6758-26b8-c9ea-4c5d] — S2: add the 429 policy in the extracted module.** Reuses
  `_errors.parse_retry_after` / `MAX_BACKOFF_S`, applies jitter-then-clamp, and scopes the retry to
  IDEMPOTENT READS behind a per-call opt-in defaulting to OFF.

**S2 `depends_on` S1** — recorded as a link, not merely stated, so `next-batch` withholds S2 until
S1 closes.

**The constraint that shapes S2, restated here because it is the one that must not be lost in the
split:** `_with_connection_retry` is the single choke point for ALL 15 transport call sites
INCLUDING `create_issue`. Retrying 429s there would REINTRODUCE the duplicate-issue class
[rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] just fixed — a 429 can arrive after the server began the write, and
nothing in the response distinguishes that from rejection at the gate.

## Scope

No code changes land under THIS ticket. Its scope is the decomposition and the two children above.

## Testing

The children carry the behavioural tests. This ticket's own verification is that the decomposition
is complete and correctly ordered — checkable from the ticket graph, not from a test run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] both children exist, are children of this ticket, and between them cover the whole original
      scope: the relocation (S1) and the 429 policy (S2), with nothing from the original plan
      orphaned
- [ ] S2 depends_on S1 as a recorded link, verified by `next-batch` withholding S2 while S1 is open
- [ ] the duplicate-risk constraint (429 retry must NOT reach mutations, because
      `_with_connection_retry` fronts `create_issue`) appears in S2's plan, so the split cannot lose
      the finding that took four review rounds to establish
- [ ] the ten-round review record stays on this ticket as comments, so the reason for the split is
      recoverable by the next reader rather than being rediscovered
- [ ] both children are CLOSED before this ticket closes
